A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KScope research work. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across the revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments characterizing nine LLMs across four datasets, feature-importance analyses, context-augmentation experiments, and supplementary results in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds noisy-context and open-ended HotpotQA evaluations, including detailed knowledge-status transitions in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The four-stage KScope procedure, response sampling, and context-augmentation methods are unchanged. Semantic clustering for open-ended responses was already specified in v1 Section 3.2; v2 evaluates that existing capability and identifies its clustering model rather than introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: The four datasets remain unchanged, but v2 substantially extends HotpotQA coverage to noisy retrieved context and open-ended answering without predefined options. V1 evaluated three-option questions, using gold supporting evidence for contextual knowledge. These additions change both input conditions and task requirements.

E2.justification: The context-augmentation comparisons retain original context, credibility enhancement, naive summarization, constrained summarization, and their combined strategy. Appendix C retains the majority-class dummy comparator for logistic regression. The additional HotpotQA evaluations reuse the existing nine target LLMs without introducing a competing characterization method.

E3.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 introduce substantial additional evaluation protocols: supplying the top ten retrieved Wikipedia paragraphs and evaluating free-form responses through semantic clustering with gemma-2-9b-it. Existing experiments retain their settings, including temperature 1, 100 responses, 20 question paraphrases, and the original regression evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: V2 adds systematic tests of sensitivity to retrieval quality and answer format across nine LLMs. Figure 5 compares these conditions, while Appendix B Figures 18–19 examine transitions from each initial knowledge status. These analyses test robustness beyond v1's gold-context multiple-choice setting; existing sensitivity and augmentation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces a different repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-reporting practice. The KScope significance threshold, Bonferroni procedures, correlation significance annotations, and response-sampling counts are retained. The additional experiments do not introduce a new statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Matched original results are unchanged, but v2 adds extensive status distributions and transition results. For Llama-8B on HotpotQA, Figure 5 newly reports 66.6% consistent-correct knowledge with noisy multiple-choice context and 88.6% with open-ended gold context, alongside the retained 95.2% for multiple-choice gold context. These are different experimental conditions, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Figure 2 retain the same knowledge-mode definition, five status conditions, empirical distribution estimator, statistical hypotheses, and hierarchical testing logic. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs accompany the added evaluations.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a principal finding that noisy retrieval and open-ended questions reduce knowledge-update effectiveness, and qualifies existing domain/model comparisons as multiple-choice results. The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion otherwise retain the taxonomy, KScope, feature-analysis, and augmentation claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving refusals and misleading context, including Gemma's increased absent knowledge without answer options. It explicitly confines the feature and augmentation analyses to gold-context multiple choice and revises the limitations after testing noisy retrieval and open-ended questions. Existing feature-based interpretations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the top-ten-paragraph input and gemma-2-9b-it clustering model for its added experiments. Existing hardware, sampling settings, regression details, appendix prompts, and code-access information are retained; the code link is relocated. Retrieval and clustering implementation details remain brief.

R1.justification: The reference list is identical, and the central novelty positioning is retained. Section 2 makes a limited substantive positioning change: the work now examines knowledge updates under both gold and noisy retrieval, whereas v1 described a gold-retrieval setting.

P1.justification: V2 consolidates the original distribution and transition discussion into Section 5.1 and organizes new Sections 5.2–5.3 around evaluation settings. It adds scope qualifications, revises limitations, and updates the publication footer. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 5, combining two retained HotpotQA distributions with three new distributions, and adds appendix transition plots in Figures 18–19. Existing plots receive explicit setting labels and revised captions, with subsequent renumbering and reflow. The established visual designs are largely retained.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly left open-ended evaluation and noisy retrieval untested despite claiming broader applicability. V2 addresses both gaps across nine LLMs in Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendix B, providing evidence of applicability and revealing important failure conditions beyond idealized evaluation. This substantially strengthens the paper's empirical support. The gains remain bounded by the HotpotQA-only extensions, brief retrieval/clustering documentation, and unchanged gold-context scope of the feature and augmentation analyses.
